ledger.claim: The fare_breakdown fixes this trip as UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of 45.00, while the same ledger records total_charged of 55.20 and refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 — so the platform billed SGD 10.20 more than the price it locked at booking. POL-RD-11 makes the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-through lines a remedy refunded in full, and on this ledger that excess is SGD 10.20.

No pass-through or statutory line can be added back to the quoted fare before that comparison: tolls_erp is 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and in any event not chargeable because this trip ENDS at Changi T3 rather than originating there, and waiting_time_fee is 0.00. The refundable excess therefore stays the whole SGD 10.20, and no POL-RD-09 correction reduces it or duplicates it.

The rider does not contend that the driver deviated, and the platform's own derived figures agree: trace_distance_km of 19.76 against optimal_distance_km of 19.6 is an excess of 0.16 km, or about 0.82%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. That is precisely why no distance-or-time refund is sought: on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 makes the quoted fare the reference, and the only live monetary question is the charge above that quote, which requires no excess to be shown.

The artifacts the rider relies on describe one and the same trip — trip_id TRP-00506 on the trip record, the trace and the ledger, with the ride starting at 04:36:40 on the record and at the trace's first fix — so the quoted figure and the charged figure are read off the same journey. Because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, the additional-corroboration overlay in POL-RD-08 is not engaged and cannot be used to demand more of this claim.

The present payment state is what the ruling has to move: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so unless a ruling returns the SGD 10.20 the rider keeps carrying it. The claim is supported as to that SGD 10.20 and unsupported as to the remainder of the SGD 55.20, which is exactly the PARTIAL_REFUND outcome POL-GEN-03 defines for a filing rider, and SGD 10.20 already sits on a 0.05 boundary so no rounding issue arises.

There is no route deviation on this trip. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test: the trace measures 19.76 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km taken from the platform's own routing-engine-v3.2 estimate. That is an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH gates to pass - more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute - and neither does: 0.16 km is a fifth of the absolute gate and 0.82% is a fortieth of the proportional gate. Even on the disfavoured rounded trip_record figure of 19.8 km the excess is only 0.20 km and 1.02%, still inside both gates. The driver drove the optimal corridor, and the rider's own claim that the route was 'same route, no stops' is therefore the accurate one.

The trace the driver's case rests on cannot be attacked on integrity grounds. It carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, running continuously from 04:36:40 to 05:00:40. None of POL-RD-07's three policy-impairment limbs fires - there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds - so the 19.76 km reading stands exactly as measured, the trace is usable for policy purposes, and no independent corroboration of the distance is required of anyone.

The rider carries the initial burden of proof under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. Limb (a) is met - TRP-00506 is the identifier on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so the artifacts do describe the same trip - but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and the measured excess is 0.16 km and 0.82%. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and the driver is not put to any exculpatory clause in answer.

The driver's account is corroborated by the record rather than contradicted by it. The trip actually ran 24.0 minutes against a booked optimal duration of 24.0 minutes; the single minute of recorded waiting was billed at 0.00 and no waiting-time fee was charged; no ERP or toll was charged at all; and the in-app chat log is complete, untruncated and contains no message of any kind, so there is no instruction of any sort on this trip. There is no detour, no additional stop and no chargeable waiting on this record to point to.

POL-RD-02 does not run on this trip and no distance-or-time refund is available. The fare model recorded on the fare breakdown is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare of SGD 45.00, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking; under POL-RD-11 the rider cannot recover on those lines however large the excess - and here the excess is not large, it is 0.16 km. The rider's premise that the price was locked in when he booked is correct, and it is precisely why there is no distance or time refund to compute against the driver's route.

The only money question left on this record is bounded by POL-RD-11(a): the increment by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable. Every pass-through on this trip is nil - ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00 (the trip ENDS at Changi, it does not originate there, so no surcharge is properly chargeable) and waiting_time_fee 0.00 - so the outer limit of any correction is the SGD 10.20 gap between the 45.00 quote and the 55.20 charge, not the 55.20 the rider has contested. That gap is a fare-model matter on the platform's own rate card and quote; no artifact attributes any part of it to the driver's driving, and it cannot ground an adverse finding against him.

There is no repeat-deviation case to answer. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation, meaning an excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km under POL-RD-01, and this trip has no deviation at all. Even if the driver profile were consulted, the only two fields POL-RD-06 names show nothing: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 250, a ratio of 0.00 against the clause's thresholds of 3 or more flags, or 0.05 or more, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under limb (b) is available, and no referral under limb (c) is warranted.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and this case should be ruled on rather than held. The trip identifier matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired even on POL-RD-07's looser policy thresholds; the timestamps run forward consistently (accepted 04:30:40, arrived 04:35:40, started 04:36:40, ended 05:00:40, trace 04:36:40 to 05:00:40); no exculpatory clause is invoked against anything absent from the pool; and every charge line has its counterpart in the trace distance, the recorded duration or the published rate card. The record is complete on every fact the ruling needs.

Profile material is credibility weighting only and may not decide anything here. Under POL-GEN-01 the only fields that can ground a decision are those a clause names for its own test; every other field is context only - the rider's rating, account age, lifetime trips and prior dispute counters, and the driver's acceptance rate, active region and his LIFETIME prior_deviation_flags counter of 0. In particular prior_deviation_flags is not deviation_flags_90d, and the driver's no_show_terminations_30d is citable only for the no-show test, which is not the dispute before this tribunal. Any argument built on those fields must be discarded, and this trip must be decided on this trip's trace.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you are right that the price you locked at booking was not the price you were charged, and that is the one thing this ruling fixes. EV-FARE-00506 records an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 45.00 against total_charged of 55.20 — an excess of 10.20. POL-RD-11(a) refunds that excess in full, less only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable on top of the quote, and on this ledger there are none: tolls_erp 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, waiting_time_fee 0.00, and airport_surcharge 0.00 — a Changi surcharge is chargeable only on a trip ORIGINATING at the airport, and this trip ended at Changi T3, so none is properly chargeable in any event. The refundable figure therefore stays the whole 10.20, and it already sits on a 0.05 boundary. The balance of the 55.20 stands. On an upfront-quoted trip the distance and time lines are fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to you however the trip was driven; your premise that the booking price was locked is correct, and it is precisely why the only money that moves is the gap above the quote. To the driver: nothing in this ruling is a finding against you. The governing trace (EV-GPS-00506, weight 1.0; 145 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0 s) measures trace_distance_km 19.76 against optimal_distance_km 19.60 — an excess of 0.16 km, or 0.82% — below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs over the rounded trip_record copy of 19.8 km, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 never runs. The 10.20 is a reconciliation between the platform's quote and the platform's own rate-card charge, not a penalty on your driving, and it is not netted against you. On the driver's-side claims: your POL-RD-01 no-deviation claim is accepted, and the same finding disposes of your POL-RD-11 claims that no distance-or-time refund is available and that the outer limit of any correction is the 10.20 gap; your POL-RD-07 claim that the trace is not policy-impaired is accepted (no limb (a)-(c) fires); your POL-RD-08 claim that the rider's threshold burden is not discharged is accepted and is consistent with this outcome, since the money moved rests on the quote/charge comparison, which requires no excess; your POL-RD-06 claim is accepted — no MATERIAL deviation exists, and even on the named fields driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is established, no limb (b) uplift is available and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is warranted; your POL-RD-10 claim is accepted — identifiers match, timestamps run forward, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact, and every charge line has its counterpart — so no escalation trigger fires and the case is ruled rather than held. The rider's POL-RD-11 claim for the 10.20 excess is accepted and is the ruling; the rider's POL-RD-09/POL-RD-11 claim that no pass-through line is added back is accepted; the rider's POL-RD-08 claim that the artifacts describe one trip and that the deviation_claims_60d overlay is not engaged is accepted. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance of 19.8 km is not less than the traced 19.76 km, so POL-RD-04's unbilled-distance limb has no shortfall to compute, and no gantry or surcharge line fails POL-RD-09(4), so there is no billing-integrity referral. Driver compensation is null. On the profiles: EV-DPROF-00506 and EV-RPROF-00506 were used only as credibility context. Their rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rates, acceptance rate, active region and the lifetime counters prior_deviation_flags and prior_disputes_filed are context-only under POL-GEN-01 and decided nothing; only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d (POL-RD-06) and deviation_claims_60d (POL-RD-08) were consulted, and neither side's near-synonym arguments were given weight. EV-ADVIS-00506-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0; it carries no fact, no exculpatory clause was invoked against it, and POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not engaged. The ruling rests on EV-FARE-00506 at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
